summary: Plan joined-up public services with blueprints, interoperability mapping and practical roadmaps. Explore the course and strengthen your delivery approach.
lede: Digital public service delivery and interoperability training helps government teams plan joined-up services across agencies. It is for digital-government leads, social-protection teams and programme architects. Participants map service journeys and handoffs, assess identity and payment dependencies, and plan accessible online and assisted channels. They also document data-sharing safeguards and build implementation roadmaps with progress measures through service-blueprinting and process-mapping exercises.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who shape or operate digital public services, especially where social-protection delivery depends on coordination across agencies, systems and service channels.
prerequisites: Prior experience in public-service delivery, social-protection programmes, government ICT, programme design or a related operational role is recommended. No coding is required. The course addresses interoperability and privacy methods at operational planning level, not technical implementation level. Bring a laptop with Excel access for spreadsheet-based exercises.
